title: Livestock and agriculture for family livelihoods
subtitle: Goat rearing, pig rearing and beekeeping
summary: The livelihoods programme worked through women’s groups to strengthen household income through goats, pigs and beekeeping. It directly supported 50 families. The project team reports that more than 26 of those families moved out of poverty. The work also aimed to ease financial pressures within households and contribute to the prevention of domestic violence.

pages.heading: Income generation through women’s groups
paragraphs: Anchored Bridges Initiatives (ABI), formerly Ability Beyond the Iris, worked with supporters to provide livelihood opportunities that families could develop within their communities. Support focused on productive assets and small enterprises that could be managed locally.

Women’s groups received support for goat rearing, pig rearing and beekeeping. These activities were intended to help families generate income and improve their ability to meet everyday needs. The women’s role as producers and organisers was central to the programme.
pages.after: The reported reach was 50 directly supported families, with more than 26 families reported to have moved out of poverty.

pages.heading: Goats and pigs as household assets
paragraphs: The photographic archive shows women with goats, livestock shelters and pig-rearing activities. Together, these images document the practical setting in which households cared for their animals and developed income-generating activities.

The programme’s livelihood objective was to help families build a more reliable economic base. Its wider social aim was to reduce financial strain and support safer family relationships, alongside efforts to prevent domestic violence.

pages.heading: Beekeeping and continued family support
paragraphs: Beekeeping complemented the livestock activities. The archive includes traditional hives among trees and a project visit to a beekeeping site. These photographs provide a record of the activity alongside the goats and pigs shown elsewhere in the report.

The reported progress of more than 26 families provides a reason to continue supporting women’s economic opportunities. Future support can build on the same focus on household livelihoods while following how income and family wellbeing develop over time.
pages.after: We thank the women’s groups, participating families, ABI and the supporters who made these livelihood opportunities possible.

title: School solidarity between Bendorf and Uganda
subtitle: Learning materials, accessible school routes and Christmas gifts
period: Historical project report with photographs from 2017 and 2018
summary: Pupils at Wilhelm-Remy-Gymnasium Bendorf raised approximately €7,000 to support fellow learners in Uganda through Anchored Bridges Initiatives (ABI), formerly Ability Beyond the Iris. Their support helped provide school materials and Christmas gift boxes and finance two access ramps at Royal College Namugongo. The partnership also brought learning about Uganda into English classes in Bendorf.

pages.heading: Pupils supporting fellow learners
paragraphs: The partnership connected pupil-led fundraising in Germany with practical support delivered through ABI in Uganda. A cheque-handover photograph records the pupils’ contribution, while photographs from Uganda show school materials being handed to students by ABI team members in white T-shirts.

Royal College Namugongo is the secondary school and parent school of Royal Junior Namugongo. The older students in white school shirts shown in the handover photographs belong to Royal College. The school-fee support for six pupils at Royal Junior is described separately.
pages.after: The approximately €7,000 was a shared fundraising pool supporting the school partnership, the Rwengoma Primary School feeding initiative and six Royal Junior pupils’ fees. The latter two activities are described in separate reports.

pages.heading: Learning about Uganda in Bendorf
paragraphs: The exchange extended beyond fundraising. Pupils prepared and displayed information about Uganda, its culture and the work of ABI. The photograph named 20170624_163328.jpg records one of these displays in an English classroom in Bendorf on 24 June 2017.

The school’s English department also describes using the Uganda partnership in selected classes to support intercultural learning. The classroom work gave pupils a setting in which to discuss their counterparts and connect their learning with the practical support they were organising.
pages.source: School context: Wilhelm-Remy-Gymnasium Bendorf, English department, https://wrg-online.de/englisch

pages.heading: School materials and accessible entrances
paragraphs: Donated funds helped finance two ramps at Royal College Namugongo. The photographs document a ramp with metal railings and a second concrete entrance ramp. These changes were intended to make school routes easier to use for students with mobility disabilities.

The partnership also supplied scholastic materials. An ABI team member is shown giving books to a student using a wheelchair. A separate handover photograph records a cheque for UGX 1,000,000 to Royal College Namugongo, dated 18 September 2018, documenting one contribution within the wider support.

pages.heading: Christmas gift boxes shared across the partnership
paragraphs: Pupils in Germany also prepared Christmas gift boxes for their counterparts in Uganda. The project account identifies books, shoes, pens, colouring materials and pencils among the donated items.

The photographs show wrapped boxes in Germany and recipients in Uganda displaying boxes and their contents. These personal contributions complemented the school materials and accessibility work. They gave pupils a direct way to take part in the partnership and support fellow learners.
pages.after: We thank the pupils and staff of Wilhelm-Remy-Gymnasium Bendorf, the participating schools in Uganda, ABI and all supporters who helped turn the pupils’ fundraising and gifts into practical educational support.

title: Mobility aids for participation in Uganda
subtitle: Two containers supporting access to school, work and community life
summary: In 2018, the initiative mobilised two 40-foot containers of mobility equipment and distributed aids to more than 600 beneficiaries in Ntungamo, Jinja and Kasubi. Working with ABI, Crutches for Africa and individual supporters in Germany, the project connected donated equipment with people who needed it for everyday movement, education and work.

pages.heading: From donated equipment to local distribution
paragraphs: The equipment included crutches, walking frames, wheelchairs and walking aids for people with visual impairments. The photographic archive shows an open container, equipment being made available and children and adults gathered with mobility aids.

Anchored Bridges Initiatives (ABI), formerly Ability Beyond the Iris, worked with partners and supporters to organise the support in Uganda. Crutches for Africa and individual supporters in Germany contributed to the wider collaboration.

pages.heading: Practical support for individual users
paragraphs: Distribution involved people with different mobility needs. The photographs show crutch support, wheelchair users and adjustments to a wheelchair during a distribution activity. They record the practical work that accompanied making the equipment available.
The reported reach of more than 600 people covers the initiative across Ntungamo, Jinja and Kasubi. Local distribution brought the equipment closer to the communities it was intended to serve.

pages.heading: Reported changes in education and work
paragraphs: The project account describes substantial changes for many recipients. School-going beneficiaries were better able to return to school, while working adults could resume work or continue it with greater ease. The equipment also supported participation in everyday family and community activities.

These reported experiences show why mobility support matters beyond the handover of an aid. The purpose was to help people pursue their education, livelihoods and daily responsibilities with fewer physical barriers.
pages.after: We thank the recipients, ABI, Crutches for Africa, the individual supporters in Germany and the other partners who helped make the 2018 distributions possible.

title: Craft enterprise for women with disabilities
subtitle: Supporting income, employment and access to markets
period: Ongoing support from 2018 with earlier archival photographs
summary: Since 2018, the organisation has supported women living with different disabilities to develop income and employment through craft production. Working with ABI, the initiative has supported a small number of producers, purchased their products and helped find buyers in Europe. Its focus is on recognising women as skilled producers and strengthening opportunities for paid work.

pages.heading: Skills and enterprise within the community
paragraphs: Women with disabilities can face barriers when seeking paid employment. This initiative responds by supporting craft-based livelihoods and helping producers reach customers for their work. The photographic archive shows sewing, handmade bags and smaller craft products.

Anchored Bridges Initiatives (ABI), formerly Ability Beyond the Iris, is the partner organisation in Uganda. The archive includes craft photographs taken in July 2017. They provide an earlier visual record of the craft activity, while the ongoing support described in this report dates from 2018.

pages.heading: Buying products and developing markets
paragraphs: Support has included buying craft products from producers and seeking markets for them in Europe. Purchasing the work gives practical value to the producers’ skills and connects the support to demand for their products.

The organisation continues to buy products and intends to feature selected items in its forthcoming online shop. This planned shop will provide another way for supporters to discover the producers’ work.

Please support this work by choosing products made by the participating women when they become available and by helping connect their work with new customers. Continued interest in the products can help broaden opportunities for income and employment.
pages.after: We thank the producers, ABI, customers and supporters who continue to value these skills and help build access to markets.

title: Supporting school meals at Rwengoma Primary
subtitle: A contribution to school lunches and a vegetable garden initiative
period: Historical project report with a contribution recorded in October 2018
summary: Through ABI, the initiative contributed UGX 1,000,000 to Rwengoma Primary School to support its lower primary lunch programme and its plan to establish a school vegetable garden. The contribution came from the approximately €7,000 raised by pupils at Wilhelm-Remy-Gymnasium Bendorf. It responded to concerns that hunger was among the reasons pupils were leaving school.

pages.heading: A contribution towards school meals
paragraphs: Rwengoma Primary School is a public school whose limited funds made it difficult to sustain school lunches. The project account identifies hunger as one of several reasons for pupils dropping out. The contribution supported the school’s own initiative to improve its food provision.

Anchored Bridges Initiatives (ABI), formerly Ability Beyond the Iris, delivered the support through the partnership. The handover cheque photographed with school representatives records UGX 1,000,000 and bears the date 11 October 2018.
pages.after: The UGX 1,000,000 contribution was an allocation from the approximately €7,000 raised by the Bendorf pupils. The wider school partnership and the school-fee support are covered in companion reports.

pages.heading: A vegetable garden to support the lunch programme
paragraphs: The school’s proposed vegetable garden linked the contribution to a practical source of food for its lunch programme. The aim was to strengthen the school’s ability to provide meals for lower primary pupils and address hunger as a barrier to staying in school.

The contribution supported a locally identified priority: helping the school strengthen its lunch programme through vegetable growing. Improved food provision and keeping pupils in school were the central objectives of the initiative.

The project illustrates how pupil-led fundraising in Germany could support a locally identified priority in Uganda. We thank the pupils and staff in Bendorf, the Rwengoma school community and ABI for their part in the initiative.

title: School fee support for six Royal Junior pupils
subtitle: Helping pupils complete primary school and progress to secondary education
summary: Six pupils at Royal Junior Namugongo received school-fee support when their families could not fully finance their education. Support was delivered through ABI using funds raised by pupils at Wilhelm-Remy-Gymnasium Bendorf. The project account reports that all six pupils completed primary education and progressed to secondary school.

pages.heading: Keeping education within reach
paragraphs: School costs can interrupt a child’s education when a family cannot meet the full fees. The initiative helped meet those costs for six Royal Junior pupils so that financial pressure did not bring their primary schooling to an early end.

Anchored Bridges Initiatives (ABI), formerly Ability Beyond the Iris, supported the pupils through its local partnership. Royal Junior Namugongo is distinct from Royal College Namugongo, the secondary and parent school. The older students in white shirts in the companion school report belong to Royal College.

pages.heading: Pupil fundraising supporting continued learning
paragraphs: The school-fee support formed part of the AktionsWerk pupil-led fundraising project. It drew on the same approximately €7,000 fundraising pool that also supported school materials, accessibility work and the Rwengoma feeding initiative.
The project team reports that all six supported pupils completed primary school and joined secondary education. Their continued learning was the central outcome of the fee support.
We thank the pupils and staff of Wilhelm-Remy-Gymnasium Bendorf, the families and school communities, ABI and everyone who helped the six pupils continue their education.
